samples.summary: `saveSnapshot()` moved inside `doc.batch()` suppresses the pre-edit caret presence write that undo relies on
samples.evidence: `handleTab` (2703-2706), `handleIndent` (2763-2765) and `handleOutdent` (2780-2782) now call `this.saveSnapshot()` *inside* `this.doc.batch(...)`. In `editor.ts` the `saveSnapshot` closure handed to `TextEditor` is not just `docStore.snapshot()` — it also calls `setCursorForHistory(cursor.position, selection…)` (editor.ts:2539-2551). Under `YorkieDocStore`, `setCursorForHistory` → `updateCursorPos`, which at yorkie-doc-store.ts:3179 does `if (this.skipNonHistoryPresence()) return;` and `skipNonHistoryPresence()` is `this.activeRoot !== null` — true for the whole batch. So the pre-edit caret/selection is never published before the change, and the reverse presence Yorkie records for the batch is whatever the live-cursor publisher happened to leave behind. The repo documents exactly this constraint elsewhere: editor.ts:3710-3715 keeps its `setCursorForHistory` "*outside* the batch, unlike the snapshot: `YorkieDocStore` holds a non-history presence write back while a batch is open, so the pre-edit caret would never reach presence at all." Result: Cmd+Z after Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ can restore the document but not the pre-edit caret+selection (the #523-class bug). Only the collaborative store is affected; `MemDocStore` has no presence.

samples.summary: A refused subtree also swallows every selected item inside it, so legal moves in the selection are silently dropped
samples.evidence: `planSiblingGroup` marks the whole subtree `covered` (line 90) *before* the boundary checks (93-94) and `continue`s on refusal, so any other selected item inside that subtree is skipped even when it could move. Two reachable consequences, both behaviour regressions against the previous per-item loop: (a) outdent — select a whole list whose first item is at level 0 (Ctrl+A, Shift+Tab) and the gesture is now a complete no-op; previously the nested items flattened. Asserted deliberately by the new test (`plan(blocks, ['a','b'], -1)` → `{}`), so it is a designed trade-off, but it is a user-visible loss of a common gesture. (b) indent — levels `a0(selected), b1, c8, d1(selected)`: `subtreeOf(a)` reaches `c` so `deepest === 8` and the whole run is refused, and `d` (which could legally indent on its own) is covered and skipped. Nothing tests case (b) and it is not obviously intended.

samples.summary: `siblingsOf` uses throwing `getBlock` where the editor.ts twin deliberately uses `findBlock`
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` resolves the parent table with `this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId)`, which throws `Block not found` when the id is stale. The parent map comes from `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`, which is only as fresh as the last layout pass. The equivalent helper added in the same change (editor.ts:1636-1645) explicitly avoids this: "Resolved with `findBlock`, not `getBlock`: the map is only as fresh as the last layout pass, so a table removed since then would throw out of the middle of an indent gesture rather than degrade to the block alone." Here the throw would escape from inside `doc.batch()` in `handleTab`/`handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` and out of the keydown handler.

samples.summary: A missing/stale `blockParentMap` entry makes the whole indent gesture a silent no-op instead of moving the block
samples.evidence: `siblingsOf` returns `doc.getContextBlocks()` when `cellInfo` is undefined, and `cell?.blocks ?? [block]` otherwise. `planSiblingGroup` only ever plans blocks it finds *inside* the handed array (list-level.ts:84-87). If the caret sits on a cell-internal block created since the last layout pass (the map is rebuilt only in `recomputeLayout`, editor.ts:1573-1580), `cellInfo` is undefined, the top-level context array is handed instead, the block's id is never matched, and indent/outdent do nothing at all. The same holds if `cellInfo` is stale and points at a cell that no longer contains the block. The old code did `fn(block)` and indented unconditionally, so this is a new failure mode; it fails silently rather than loudly.

mergedFrom.summary: `siblingsOf` calls `doc.getBlock(cellInfo.tableBlockId)`, which throws when the parent map is stale, turning an indent gesture into an uncaught exception

finding.summary: editor.ts `siblingsOf` resolves cell parentage from the body-only `layout.blockParentMap`, so indent/outdent silently no-ops for a list item inside a header/footer table cell
finding.evidence: `forEachBlockInSelection`'s cursor-only fallback (editor.ts:1711) reads `layout.blockParentMap`, which is the BODY layout's map (`layout` is assigned only from `computeLayout(doc.document.blocks, …)` at editor.ts:1523; header/footer cell parentage lives in `headerLayout`/`footerLayout` and is merged only into `doc.setBlockParentMap` at editor.ts:1573-1580 — the comment at editor.ts:3350 documents exactly this body-only limitation). For a caret in a header/footer table cell, `cellInfo` is therefore `undefined`, so `siblingsOf` returns `doc.getContextBlocks()` (the header's TOP-LEVEL blocks). The cell block's id is not in that array, so `planSiblingGroup` never matches it and `planListLevelChanges` returns an empty plan — `editor.indent()`/`outdent()` change no list level at all. Before this change the fallback called `fn(block)` and the level was written by id, so the gesture worked. `text-editor.ts`'s `siblingsOf` avoids this by using `getActiveLayout()` via `getCellInfo` (text-editor.ts:3650); editor.ts should use the merged `doc.blockParentMap` instead.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim is false in this working tree. `siblingsOf` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1636-1645) reads no parent map itself; it receives `cellInfo` as an argument. Its sole call site (editor.ts:1733) obtains that argument at editor.ts:1732 from `doc.blockParentMap.get(block.id)` — the MERGED body+header+footer map — not from the body-only `layout.blockParentMap`. The merged map is built and installed in `recomputeLayout` at editor.ts:1573-1580 (`mergedParentMap` seeded from `layout.blockParentMap` then overlaid with `headerLayout.blockParentMap` and `footerLayout.blockParentMap`, then `doc.setBlockParentMap(mergedParentMap)`; setter at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:112-117). Therefore a caret inside a header/footer table cell does resolve `cellInfo`, `siblingsOf` returns the cell's `blocks`, and the indent/outdent plan can match the block — the alleged no-op path does not exist. The specific line the reviewer cites as the offending read, editor.ts:1711, is `for (const row of b.tableData.rows)` inside the top-level multi-block selection branch, not a `blockParentMap` lookup. The only `layout.blockParentMap` reads in `forEachBlockInSelection` are editor.ts:1683-1684, which belong to the same-cell cross-block SELECTION branch and are not on the cursor-only fallback path the finding describes. The remediation the finding asks for ("editor.ts should use the merged `doc.blockParentMap`") is already implemented and documented in-code at editor.ts:1624-1630 and 1729-1731. Verified packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts is the only file at the cited path (the other `view/editor.ts` is in packages/notes, a different package).

finding.summary: Carrying children turns one indent gesture into N separate store writes without `Doc.batch()`, so under YorkieDocStore each carried child is its own undo/CRDT unit and Cmd+Z leaves the subtree half-moved
finding.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` loops `doc.setBlockType(...)` once per planned block (editor.ts:1600-1611; identical loops in text-editor.ts:2717-2722 and text-box-editor.ts:826-831). `Doc.setBlockType` issues one `store.setBlockType` + `refresh()` per call, and `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` opens its own `withUpdate` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1535) — i.e. one Yorkie change and one `doc.history` entry per block, since only `batch()` collapses writes into a single undo unit (yorkie-doc-store.ts:567-574). `Doc.batch()` exists (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:146) and is not used here. Previously a single-caret indent was exactly one write; now a parent with k children is k+1 undo steps, and each intermediate undo state is precisely the parent-at-child-level corruption this PR exists to prevent (the same failure mode called out in document.ts:407-419 for Backspace). Remote peers also observe the intermediate states.

verdict.reason: The finding's core premise — that `applyListLevelChanges`'s per-block `setBlockType` loop runs without `Doc.batch()` — is false in this tree. All six call sites are wrapped in a batch: editor.ts:3605-3614 (`indent`) and 3624-3635 (`outdent`); text-editor.ts:2703-2706 (`handleTab`), 2763-2772 (`handleIndent`), 2780-2791 (`handleOutdent`); text-box-editor.ts:1170-1179 (`indent`) and 1188-1199 (`outdent`). A Grep for `applyListLevelChanges(` returns exactly those 6 invocations plus the 3 definitions, so no path reaches the loop unbatched (text-box-editor has no separate Tab handler). The batching seam also behaves as the finding says is required: `YorkieDocStore.batch` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2876-2916) opens a single `doc.update` and sets `activeRoot`, and `withUpdate` (2866-2874), the path used by `setBlockType` (1535), reuses that ambient root rather than opening a nested update — so the N writes collapse into one Yorkie change and one `doc.history` entry, and `docStore.snapshot()` is a documented no-op inside a batch. `Document.batch` (document.ts:146-153) is the wrapper the editors call. Hence there is no k+1-undo-step or half-moved-subtree behavior as described.
